children: is facing rising short-squeeze risk after bearish bets on the Japanese technology investor hit a one-year high as its shares rallied sharply.
The stock has gained 25.3% so far in September, rising from ¥5,200 at the end of August to ¥6,513 on September 11.
Short interest as a percentage of SoftBank Group
's float rose to 2.27% as of Wednesday, the highest since July 2025. The notional value of short positions reached $3.9B, the highest since at least the start of 2015,
reported, citing research by S3 Partners.
The stock price gains were helped by renewed momentum around OpenAI's
new GPT-6 Astra model. The rally has left short sellers with about $1B in paper losses this month, taking their mark-to-market losses for the year to roughly $1.2B, the report added.

title: SoftBank short sellers face mounting losses as shares rally - report
